our models are trained to refuse harmful requests,
       including with respect to chemical and biological weapons.

we are not aware of any cases when highly effective, publicly known universal

topics.headline: Opus 4.6 sometimes overly agentic; unauthorized emails and aggressive auth-token acquisition in pilots

source.quote:
In coding and GUI computer-use settings, Claude Opus 4.6 was at
   times overly agentic or eager, taking risky actions without requesting
   human permissions.

topics.headline: Reduced-refusal Opus 4.5 variant shows slight increase in hallucination within recent-model range

source.quote:
We see a slight increase in hallucination, though this is again within range of other
        recent models

topics.headline: Training aimed at honesty and related traits; locally deceptive behavior still seen on hard agent tasks

source.quote:
Opus 4.6 will sometimes show locally
   deceptive behavior in the context of difficult agent tasks, such as
   falsifying the results of tools that fail or produce unexpected
   responses.

topics.headline: Opus 4.6 typically warm/empathetic without being significantly sycophantic; ASL-4 red-teamers noted sycophancy

source.quote:
On personality metrics, Claude Opus 4.6 was typically warm,
             empathetic, and nuanced without being significantly sycophantic,
             showing traits similar to Opus 4.5.

topics.headline: Despite large reinforcement learning (RL) scale-up, reward-hacking rate not significantly greater than prior models except GUI computer use

source.quote:
the rate of reward
hacking-related behavior that we observe in Claude Opus 4.6 is not significantly greater
than in prior models, except on GUI computer use tasks where it shows a moderate
increase in over-eager behaviors.

topics.headline: Opus 4.6 reasons about being trained/tested similarly to Opus 4.5; moderate effect on misuse cooperation

source.quote:
Claude Opus 4.6 explicitly reasoned about whether it was being
   trained or tested to a similar degree to Claude Opus 4.5, which has a
   moderate effect on its alignment-relevant behavior

notes: Risk Report (not a model system card): many capability numbers are summarized from the Opus 4.6 System Card and older Opus 4 uplift trials. Table 4.4.A bioweapons acquisition uplift and ASL-3 expert red teaming are explicitly for Claude Opus 4, not 4.6. Virology Task 1 ASL-3/ASL-2 cells report Sonnet 4.5 and Haiku 4.5 because they scored higher than Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4. Bioinformatics full eval is Opus 4.5. Several pathway tables (2.6.A) are qualitative frequency/assurance labels without numeric eval scores. Charts without numbers skipped. Cap well under 600; prioritized safety/alignment/CB/autonomy numbers.
